learned_patterns.pattern: The Signal Engine has not produced a fresh matrix since 2026-06-30 12:21 PDT — no 07-01 or 07-02 run fired, and 07-01/07-02-AM sessions appear skipped. SAFE MODE has now persisted for multiple consecutive sessions, blocking all signal-based action. The §2.5 staleness guard keeps CLU safe, but the workflow cron/runner reliability is the single highest-value fix on the board.

A broad semiconductor flush (SOXX -12.9% over two sessions) hit every semi name together (INTC -11%, AMD -11%, MU -7%, NVDA -6% cumulative) while VOO stayed ~flat — confirming ETF diversification buffers single-name shocks (§13.1). The tightly-set NVDA stop (5%, high-failure-risk) is now the binding constraint at +2.4%, exactly the trade-off of a tight stop: less loss if it breaks, more whipsaw risk in a sector-wide dip. Concentration in one sector (LAB+SOXX all semi) is the real exposure.

The prior pattern (composites lagging a sharp reversal) now cuts the other way: the 06-30 matrix read NEUTRAL/mildly-bullish (INTC gate was 5/5 at entry) right before a two-day -12.9% semi reversal. Stale signal is worse than lagging signal — a 2-day-old matrix cannot see a regime change. Reinforces the §2.5 no-trade-on-stale rule and the value of a same-session engine run.

Two down sessions barely moved the tier mix (LAB 25.7 / CORE 50.0 / DRIP 23.9 vs 20/50/30) because the drawdown hit LAB and CORE roughly proportionally while DRIP (JEPQ) held better. LAB stays ~5.7pp over its 20% cap; it dilutes only via base growth or a natural exit (§17.3), never a forced trim. DRIP remains the -6.1pp underweight next-deposit target.

MU fell ~16% in two sessions (from $1,164 to $976), moving from 'above entry zone, do not chase' to 'below zone, possible falling knife' — a reminder that a stale watchlist ranking is actively misleading in a fast tape. Top-3 must be re-ranked on a FRESH matrix; the current ranking is carried only as a stale planning placeholder.
